theme: piano, organ, bass and brushed drums

sections.name: Hook — MUS-OPEN
lines: I'm seventy-one, and I take the stairs
faster than women half my age.
Last Sunday, my daughter walked behind me
the whole way up and said,
"Mama, when did that happen?"

sections.name: The low point and what failed — MUS-EXPOSE
lines: Six weeks ago, I was going down my stairs backwards.
One step at a time.
I ain't gonna lie,
some days I wasn't going down them at all.
I'd just stay upstairs.
That big knee brace I bought
slid right down my leg.
By evening, it was around my ankle.
I done tried everything.
Physical therapy. Pain pills. Cortisone shots.
Every brace and sleeve they make.
Nothing worked. Nothing lasted.
Nothing gave me my life back.

sections.name: The turn — MUS-TURN
lines: Then my grandbaby got married in June.
My cousin Loretta was there.
She's seventy-four,
and she was out on that dance floor all night.
Electric Slide, Cupid Shuffle, all of it.
Both her knees was bone on bone too.
I always figured hers wasn't as bad as mine.
I always figured mine was past fixing.

sections.name: The reveal and payoff — MUS-TURN
lines: Loretta came to stay the week after.
She watched me at the kitchen table,
going through my morning routine.
Two anti-inflammatories, the gel, the brace,
an ice pack on my right knee.
After a minute she said,
"Baby, can I show you something?"
She pulled up her pant leg.
She had on a little black strap,
right under her kneecap.
Stryde.
She handed me one.
It looked ridiculous. Too small.
I said, "Loretta, you know good and well
this ain't gonna work on knees like mine."
She said, "Just put it on
and walk down them stairs."
I did.
Chile, the first step,
I didn't even have to hold the rail.
Not the second. Not the third.
All the way down.
Both feet. Forwards.

sections.name: Pure mechanism — MUS-EDU
lines: She said, "Everything else you tried
was made to keep you comfortable
while your knee got worse.
This one fixes why it hurts."
She said, "There's one spot under the kneecap
where every step lands.
Every brace, every shot,
every pill you ever tried
treated the whole knee.
Not that spot.
That's why ain't nothing worked.
The pain is pressure. That's all it is.
This strap sits right on that spot
and takes the weight off."
First step. Pain gone.
Just like that.

sections.name: Proof and the result — MUS-AFTER
lines: Over two hundred thousand people wear one now.
Sports doctors recommend it.
Not the pharma companies. Sports doctors.
Loretta's husband wears one.
He's seventy-six, and he plays golf twice a week.
Her niece wears one when she runs track.
She's twenty-two.
I've worn mine every day for six weeks.
Under my clothes.
Don't nobody know it's there.
No pills. No gel.
No brace around my ankle by lunchtime.
Yesterday I walked to the store.
Two miles there. Two miles back.
Passed three women half my age.
Stood in that checkout line ten minutes
without shifting my weight.
Carried two bags home.
Didn't nobody help me.
When I got home, my husband said,
"You was gone a long time."
I said, "I know."

sections.name: Name, authority, objection — MUS-AFTER
lines: That was six weeks of wearing the strap.
Nothing else.
Three ladies from church already ordered one
after they watched me come down the church steps.
So I'ma just say it right here.
It's called Stryde Patellar Force Redirection.
They spent three years designing it
with orthopedic surgeons.
It's the real thing.
Not them cheap knock-offs
they be selling on Amazon
and them fake websites.

sections.name: Offer and close — MUS-OFFER
lines: The link's right down below.
Two straps for the price of one right now.
Sixty days to send them back
if they don't work.
Eleven years of knee pain.
Gone the first step I took with it on.
I bought my sister a pair that same week.
She coming Sunday.
She gon' walk up my stairs on her own.
